context: A coach motivates a teen athlete before a championship
purpose: Teach: バトン/選手権/投手/巨人/クロアチア/アルゼンチン/カリフォルニア/大地

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: いよいよ明日、世界野球選手権の決勝だな。よく眠れたか?
lines.en: Tomorrow's finally the World Baseball Championship final. Did you sleep okay?
lines.style: Steady paternal coach checking in the night before.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: あんまり…。クロアチア戦も苦しかったし、決勝の相手はアルゼンチンですよね。
lines.en: Not really. The Croatia game was rough, and the final's against Argentina, right?
lines.style: Nervous teen voice, voice trailing off with worry.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: ああ。向こうの先発投手は速球派だが、お前なら打てる。先輩から受け継いだバトンを、しっかり次へ繋げ。
lines.en: Yeah. Their starter throws heat, but you can hit him. Carry forward the baton your seniors passed to you.
lines.style: Firm coach reassurance using metaphor; calm and grounded.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: でも監督、相手の四番、カリフォルニア出身の大学生で、まるで巨人みたいな体格なんです…。
lines.en: But Coach, their cleanup hitter is a college kid from California, built like a giant.
lines.style: Teen leaking anxiety through nervous detail-dropping.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 体格は関係ない。お前は自分の足で、自分の大地を踏みしめて投げればいい。
lines.en: Size doesn't matter. Just pitch with your own feet planted on your own ground.
lines.style: Philosophical short sentences; firm grounding tone.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.style: Quiet, absorbing the words with softened voice.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: そうだ。誰のためでもない、お前自身のためのマウンドだ。胸を張って行ってこい。
lines.en: That's right. That mound is for you, no one else. Go out there proud.
lines.style: Warm decisive sendoff; coach's final push of confidence.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: はい!行ってきます、監督!
lines.en: Yes sir! I'm going out there, Coach!
lines.style: Energized teen voice cracking upward with restored fire.
